requirement_text: Applying for a bachelor's degree (Year 1) -- Follow the steps below depending on your status to find out when and where to apply: I am studying for or already have a French or European baccalaureate / I am a European Union citizen / I am not a European Union citizen and I live in a country covered by the 'Etudes en France' (Studying in France) procedure / I am not a European Union citizen and I do not live in a country covered by the 'Etudes en France' (Studying in France) procedure.
researcher_notes: PSL (Universite Paris Sciences & Lettres) is a grouping/umbrella university of several component schools (Dauphine, ENS, etc.). Its own page states four distinct applicant categories for Bachelor's Year 1, one more granular split than either Sciences Po's two-pathway or Sorbonne's three-way structure encountered elsewhere in this research: French/European-Bac / EU citizen / non-EU in an Etudes en France country / non-EU NOT in an Etudes en France country. This confirms the France background doc's point that Etudes-en-France-country status (not just EU/non-EU citizenship) is a load-bearing fact. Each category's specific expanded content sits behind an accordion UI not captured by plain-text extraction this pass -- the category list itself is the confirmed fact; per-category detail (documents, specific sub-deadlines) was not individually extracted.

requirement_text: Bachelor's at PSL are selective and target high-potential students from all backgrounds.
researcher_notes: PSL's own admissions page publishes a headline selectivity statistic not commonly stated this directly by other institutions in this corpus: 'Selectivity rate 4%' (with '85% success rate (3 years)' and '100% rate of continuation of studies' shown alongside it as 'Chiffres cles Licence'). Recorded here as context rather than as its own requirement record, since a selectivity rate is an admissions statistic, not a requirement a student must meet -- flagged so it isn't lost, not fitted into a field shape it doesn't belong in.
